title: FAMILY FINANCE
mv: There is desirable treasure, And oil in the dwelling of the wise, But a foolish man squanders it.
mvp: “There is desirable treasure, And oil in the dwelling of the wise, But a foolish man squanders it.” Proverbs 21:20 (NKJV)
assignment: Plan your finance for one month and try to follow through with it. (No mark).

b.x: Finance impacts every aspect of family life, marriage, parenting, relationships, home and future stability (Ecclesiastes 10:19). Money can either build or break families depending on how it is managed. God wants families to be financially wise, disciplined and aligned with kingdom values. In this lesson, we want to explore some biblical principles for managing family resources wisely.

Everything belongs to God (Psalm 24:1; 1 Chronicles 29:11-12). Human beings manage God’s resources on His behalf (Genesis 2:15). God gives the ability to make wealth (Deuteronomy 8:18). Therefore, we must put God first and be accountable to Him in all that we do (Matthew 6:33; Romans 14:12). Parents should know and acknowledge that God is the ultimate provider (Psalm 145:15-16). Also, it is essential to know that our jobs, businesses, and skills are merely channels, not the source (1 Corinthians 4:7; James 1:17). We should learn to start every financial plan with prayer, thanksgiving, and commitment of resources to God (Philippians 4:6).

Families must plan, budget, and set priorities under God’s guidance (Luke 14:28-30). Families that fail to plan often live in a state of constant lack or debt (Proverbs 21:5). A written budget helps avoid waste and droughts. Like Joseph, families should save during the seasons of abundance (Genesis 41:47-49).

True financial peace comes from contentment and trust in God, not money (1 Timothy 6:6-10; Hebrews 13:5). Debt can enslave a family and limit what God can do through them (Proverbs 22:7; 2 Kings 4:1-7). Many families suffer because of the pressure to “keep up with others.” Avoid the grandstand lifestyle which can result in stress from overspending on luxuries or taking loans for non-essential items (Romans 13:8). Avoid debt for consumption; if a loan must be taken, let it be for a productive venture that can bring income in the future.

Finances should not divide the home; unity is essential (Amos 3:3). Mutual love, agreement and integrity are needed to achieve harmony in financial matters. Husbands and wives should agree on priorities and operate with transparency. There should be joint discussions on spending, savings, and investments; they should avoid secrecy and financial infidelity. What God has joined together, let no finances put asunder!

Financial discipline should start from the home; hence, Parents should teach their children financial values e.g. earning, giving, saving, and spending (Proverbs 22:6). Also, Parents should intentionally model good financial habits to their children (Deuteronomy 6:7). Parents should teach and practice the acts of giving and generosity. Families that honour God with their substance experience His blessing (Luke 6:38; 2 Corinthians 9:7). Encourage family giving projects to - hospitals, orphanages, the needy, Church or missions - as a way of teaching stewardship and compassion.
Managing family finance requires wisdom, discipline, cooperation and reliance on God.
